correctness.rationale: The rate balance is w b(m)p_m=d(m+1)p_(m+1); telescoping gives the stated size-site formula, and g(0)=0 fixes the increment at site zero. The polynomial product gap b(m)-d(m)>b(0) for m≥1 follows from d(0)=0 and a strictly positive coefficient of positive degree when r≥2. Induction using a_m d(m)=a_(m-1)b(m-1) proves T_m<T_0 for m≥1, while T_m>1/b(m) there. For the signed increment coefficients, the region j<m has strictly negative limiting coefficients, the site j=m has limit 1/b(m)>0, and the entire remaining tail has one sign with total converging to T_(m-1)-T_m. This gives H_m=1/b(m)+max(0,T_(m-1)-T_m)<T_0: if the max term is positive use T_m>1/b(m), and otherwise use strict growth of b. For uniformity choose the split m(1-w)≤1 or >1. In the first regime w^(-m)≤e^2 for w≥1/2 and the factor is O((m+1)/b(m)); in the second, the degree bound and geometric moments give G_(m+1)/p_m=O((1-w)^(-1))=O(m), again giving O((m+1)/b(m)). This vanishes for r≥2, and adjacent size bounds control the increment tail. A finite number of strict noninitial comparisons then yields eventual simultaneous exact maximization at site zero; the singleton and its complement attain it. All arguments include c=1 and fixed nonzero offsets. The recorded 6,156 assertions are finite evidence; the source script was not executed. A separate exact coefficient spot check at (r,c,kappa,w)=(2,1,(0,0),9/10) gives both site-zero factors 1 and the next size and increment factors 19/40 and 3/4; it is not a proof of the uniform limit.
